t: LeetCode 1958 - Check if Move is Legal
o:
**Understanding the problem**

This is Reversi move validation. Placing color on the free cell (rMove, cMove) is legal exactly when some horizontal, vertical or diagonal line through it becomes a good line with the new stone as an endpoint: your color, then one or more opponent stones, then your color again, with no free cell in between.

Examples:
- Example 1: playing B at (4, 3) caps a vertical stack of three Ws topped by a B at (0, 3), and also a W-B-B run to its left -> true.
- Example 2: the W at (4, 4) sits strictly inside good-looking patterns but never at an end -> false.

The board is permanently 8 x 8, so any exhaustive scan is constant time; clarity beats micro-optimization.
k: Legal means: walking outward in some direction from the placed cell, the immediate cells are opponents and the first non-opponent cell is your own color.
The placed stone must terminate the good line; being a middle cell disqualifies the move.
Zero trapped opponents is not enough - the line needs at least three cells including both endpoints.

a.n: Approach 1: Ray Walk in Eight Directions
a.i: March away from the move cell in each of the 8 directions while the cells show the opposite color. If at least one opponent was crossed and the next in-bounds cell equals color, the move completes a good line with (rMove, cMove) as an endpoint.
s: For each direction (dr, dc) among the 8, step once off the move cell.
Advance while in bounds and the cell equals the opposite color, counting steps.
If steps >= 1 and the following in-bounds cell equals color, return true.
Return false after all directions fail.
a.t: O(1) - 8 directions times at most 7 steps on a fixed 8 x 8 board

a.n: Approach 2: Tentatively Place, Then Scan Every Line
a.i: Write color into the move cell on a copy of the board, extract all maximal lines (8 rows, 8 columns, 15 diagonals, 15 anti-diagonals) as coordinate lists, and hunt for the pattern [color][opp+][color] whose left or right end is the move cell. Same verdict as ray walking, phrased entirely in terms of good lines.
s: Copy the board and place color at (rMove, cMove).
Collect rows, columns and both diagonal families as index lists.
On each line, from every color cell extend through consecutive opponent cells.
If the run closes on color, spans at least 3 cells, and one end is the move cell, return true.
a.t: O(1) - 46 lines of at most 8 cells scanned once each
a.sp: O(1) - the copied board and line lists

w: Deliver the ray walk - it is what interviewers expect and the shortest correct code. Call out the endpoint rule unprompted; Example 2 exists purely to punish ignoring it. Pitfalls: accepting zero trapped opponents, letting a free cell terminate a ray (it must not), and omitting one of the two diagonal families. Follow-up: list every legal move, or perform the actual flips along each winning ray.
